key_findings.finding: Reviewed human UniProt Q8TEK3 is annotated as histone-lysine N-methyltransferase, H3 lysine-79 specific; its curated function says it methylates H3 Lys79, preferentially in nucleosomes, and binds DNA. The annotation explicitly supports DOT1L/DOT1-type H3K79 methyltransferase activity.

source_tools.relevance: Direct reviewed UniProt function and activity annotations

key_findings.finding: Reviewed mouse UniProt Q6XZL8 has the same protein name and curated H3K79 methyltransferase function; it likewise prefers nucleosomal histones. Both accessions are annotated in nucleus and cytoplasm, with cytoplasmic localization dependent on MLLT6/AF17; nuclear/nucleoplasmic locations are supported by GO annotations.

source_tools.relevance: Direct reviewed UniProt function and localization annotations

key_findings.finding: Biological-process annotations include DNA damage checkpoint signaling and DNA repair for both proteins; gene expression is additionally listed for mouse. Human annotation describes SCNN1A transcriptional repression with MLLT3/AF9 following promoter H3K79 hypermethylation; mouse annotation reports the corresponding SCNN1A context. These are database annotations, not general pathway predictions.

source_tools.relevance: UniProt function and GO biological-process evidence
Mouse UniProt function and GO biological-process evidence

key_findings.finding: Pfam DOT1 family domain PF08123.20 was detected at residues 115–317 in the supplied sequence with extremely significant i-Evalue (1.1e-82); the matching mouse accession's corresponding scan reports residues 115–317 and i-Evalue 7.2e-83. This supports family/domain-level identification but is distinct from experimental functional evidence; here the reviewed UniProt function independently supports H3K79 methyltransferase activity.

source_tools.relevance: PF08123 hit and reviewed mouse annotation
